desc: LIAM (NeurIPS 2021) on URB. paper/BASELINES.md B5.
Host block == ippo/config1.json (LIAM's learner is A2C, so only lr,
entropy_coef, batch_size and the widths carry over).
embedding_dim = 20, encoder_lr = 7e-4 (lr2), max_grad_norm = 0.5
-> uoe-agents/LIAM lb_foraging/run_tests.py.
backprop_embeddings = false -> run_tests.py's default: the embedding is
DETACHED into the policy, so the encoder is trained by the
reconstruction loss alone. That separation is the method.
n_modelled = 3  LIAM's largest setting; the modelled set is the 3
nearest same-OD machine peers by departure time.
standardize_targets = true  the observation reconstruction target is
standardised per dimension. Without it URB's start-time coordinate
(order 1000, constant per traveller) is 99.99% of the squared error
and the decoder learns three constants. See CHECKLIST_liam.md
item SCALE-1 for the measurement.
MEASURED PROPERTY OF URB'S SHIPPED NETWORKS, 2026-09-19: the median
origin-destination pair carries exactly ONE traveller on all seven of them
only 0.7-3.2% of travellers ever have an EARLIER same-OD peer -- except on
ingolstadt_custom, where it is 70%. So on saint_arnoult the observation's
four count coordinates are zero for 97% of travellers on every day of the
run. Three defaults below follow from that; see the checklist item named.
graph = overlap (NOT od): a same-OD modelled set would be almost
entirely padding with the agent itself, so the decoder would
reconstruct what the encoder already has. The arm reports how
many slots were padded. See CHECKLIST_liam.md MOD-1.
